newsitem.title: CUBA: Castro says Cuba does not want "transition to hell".
newsitem.headline: Castro says Cuba does not want "transition to hell".

text.p: Cuban President Fidel Castro said on Thursday Cuba was not going to make any political transition, saying those countries that had done so had made a "transition towards hell."
Angrily rebuffing U.S. demands for political change in Cuba, Castro said countries that had done what Washington had told them to do were in chaos.

"They have made a transition towards hell, it's one of the biggest crimes in history" he said in a speech at a youth rally in Havana to mark the anniversary of a student uprising in 1957, during the rebel war that brought him to power in 1959.
Castro did not mention any country by name, but Cuban authorities generally present the transition from communism of the former East bloc countries as having been a disaster.
Castro said it was the United States, "the arrogant empire that wants to make us sheep in its flock one day," that should make a transition, "from empire to garbage bin."

His references to transition follow a White House document issued in January that outlined the foreign financial and technical aid Cuba might receive if it dumped its one-party communist system and embarked on a political transition.
Cuba angrily rejected the document and said it made its transition with the 1959 revolution.

The document was issued to comply with the Helms-Burton law that toughened Washington's longstanding economic embargo on Cuba, demanding radical political change as a condition for normal relations and also including provisions to punish some foreign companies investing in Cuba.

Castro said the law, approved by President Bill Clinton on March 12, 1996, failed to destroy Cuba's system. "A year has passed since this criminal law and we are still here and we will remain here," he said.
